attributes.size: ~378 nm in dendrite core; ~441 nm in inter-dendrite region

evidence.quote: After carefully tuning solution (1315 °C/2 h + 1320 °C/2 h + 1325 °C/2 h + 1330 °C/10 h, AC) and aging heat treatment (1120 °C/4 h, AC + 870 °C/24 h, AC), the cuboid γ’ precipitates transformed from irregularly-shaped ones are formed and their average sizes are ∼378 nm and ∼441 nm in dendrite core and inter-dendrite regions, respectively.

attributes.size: slightly increases from dendrite core to inter-dendrite region

evidence.quote: The irregularly-shaped γ’ precipi- tates can be observed in both dendrite core (DC, Fig. 3 b) and inter-dendritic region (ID, Fig. 3 c), and the measurements indicates that their average size slightly increases from the den- drite core to the inter-dendritic region.
As expected, the eutec- tic structure is readily observed in inter-dendrite region since this region is ﬁnally solidiﬁed.
The as-cast alloy is composed of typical dendritic microstruc- ture ( Fig. 3 a) on (001) plane with an average primary den- drite spacing of ∼289 μm.

attributes.location: between dendrite core and inter-dendrite region

evidence.quote: In the as-cast alloy, the experimental observations demonstrate that Os, W, Cr and Co segregate within the dendrite core and other elements segregate towards inter-dendrite region ( Fig. 4 a).

attributes.location: between dendrite core and inter-dendrite region
attributes.composition: Os k'=1.36, W k'=1.12; other elements almost homogenized

evidence.quote: Further analysis shows that segregation coeﬃcients of Os and W from dendrite core to inter-dendrite region are 2.07 and 2.02, respectively. After heat treatment, their values change to 1.36 and 1.12, respectively, while other elements are almost fully homogenized, as shown in Table 2 .
Moreover, very remarkable rafting of γ’ precipitates normal to ⟨ 001 ⟩ direction can be observed in CMSX-4 alloy after 100 h.
